title: Seq
description: Seq is a structured log server for .NET applications. It collects, stores, and displays structured logs from Serilog and other sources, providing a powerful search interface.

data.text: Seq is a self-hosted structured log server designed for .NET applications. It ingests JSON log events from Serilog, NLog, and other sources, then lets you search, filter, and visualize logs using a web interface.

data.title: Installation
data.content: Install the Serilog sink for Seq.

data.title: Sending Logs to Seq
data.content: Configure Serilog to write structured events to a local Seq instance.

terms.definition: A server that ingests structured log events and lets you search and filter by property values.
In Serilog, a destination that receives log events. Seq provides its own sink.
A filter expression used in Seq to find specific events, such as UserId = 42.

data.title: Local Development
data.text: You can run Seq locally using Docker: docker run -d --name seq -e ACCEPT_EULA=Y -p 80:80 -p 5341:5341 datalust/seq. Then open http://localhost:80 to explore logs.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Seq is a structured log server built for .NET
Serilog sends JSON events to Seq over HTTP
The Seq UI lets you filter by structured properties
data.takeaway: Seq turns raw log streams into a searchable observability dashboard.

data.title: Exercise: Ship Logs to Seq
data.description: Send structured logs from a console app to a running Seq instance.
steps: Create a console app and add the Serilog.Sinks.Seq package
Configure Serilog to write to http://localhost:5341
Log events with structured properties: OrderId, CustomerName, Amount
Open the Seq UI and run a query filtering by Amount > 100
data.expectedOutcome: Seq displays structured events that you can filter and search by property.
